extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: The largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data across a wide variety of languages, domains, and time periods.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was assembled from six main collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic. Data was collected on a resource-by-resource basis using APIs, standard retrieval methods, and large dumps from Collections As Data (CAD) initiatives.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include SEC, WTO, AMF, TED EU Tenders, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, USPTO, UN Digital Library, Collections As Data (CAD), Internet Archive, Delpher, OpenAlex, The Stack v1 and v2, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PII was replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Documents containing harmful language were either removed or synthetically rewritten without the harmful language. Highly deteriorated OCR content was synthetically rewritten using the OCRonos model.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation was performed using Segmentext. OCR error detection was conducted using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr. Code data was filtered to remove non-desired languages/formats, non-permissive licenses, and files with 75% or more digits; sequences of [\r]+\n were replaced with \n, and line lengths were recalculated.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext, OCRoscope, OCRerrcr, OCRonos, Microsoft Presidio, Celadon
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses were present in the raw data but were identified and replaced with fictitious values.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to support the pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs by making it legal to release the source data without relying on fair use. It contributes to the AI Commons and demonstrates that open LLM research is possible while meeting strict legal and regulatory requirements.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset contains historical periodicals and monographs from at least 80 years ago, which may contain cultural norms, biases, and harmful language regarding ethnic groups, women, and violence that do not meet modern ethical standards.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover the entire range of available open data (the open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. The 2 trillion tokens are suitable for pre-training limited-size models, but larger models require more data. It is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. Curation methods (e.g., OCR correction, toxicity filtering) do not have 100% accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models, developing vision-language models (VLMs) for document segmentation, developing models with legal knowledge, training models for creative writing, developing historical language models, and creating ethical fine-tuning datasets.
